having grown up in the miami valley which is right next to the old great black swamp area that *was* actually drained and the environment (esp Lake Erie) forever after devastated in favor of agriculture: yeag.
“Drain the swamp”? At this point, the swamp is about as deep as Lake Superior.

I’d choose the “great” black swamp (because I grew up in it) ~ a massive wetland connected to the Great Lakes that was settled and drained in the mid-to-late 1800s. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_B...

Excited to have written about Patrick Wensink's "The Great Black Swamp" (.bsky.social), a charming look at the unintended consequences reshaping the land, for Great Lakes Review. greatlakesreview.org/the-price-of...
i live in a literal swamp. Its like venice, if it were just swamps. we get wind off the great lakes too, which look like this.

"drain the swamp" is such a funny way to say you're going to fix things because colonizing dipshits draining swamps caused ecological disasters. Please god stop draining the swamps. The algae in lake erie is gaining sentience.

YES I talk about the Great Black Swamp draining all the time as a reason for W. Erie HABs: "Lake Erie has endured multiple anthropogenic stressors since European settlement in the area, most notably the draining of coastal wetlands for development of agricultural lands in the late 18th century"
Comparisons to a swamp are insulting to swamps everywhere. Lake Erie in the 70s, would be more accurate. Don’t smoke near it.
Oh, especially if it’s a fire swamp. I grew up next to Lake Superior and there were swamps everywhere. When I was a kid it was my favorite place to play. I still think of a swamp as a magical place.
Swan to litter the swamp unfortunately. Great lakes are shrinking in water depth, not a very good sign for anything.
